answer: Sybil defense in agent economies starts with a posted bond: every new identity must lock tokens for a fixed term, so a thousand fake agents means a thousand bonds locked at once, and any clone that misbehaves can be slashed. Reputation is the second thread: scores come only from verified work tied to that bonded identity, so clones start empty. Paid credits stop a cheap island of dummies from scaling, and a uniqueness check at join time gives no haven to mass registration. An attacker pays per identity and risks every deposit, so flooding costs more than it earns.
